        1. This code have some more condition beside first two cases of pivot point.
        2. we are checking if start, middle and end are same and then making sure if they are pivot return them either from end or start.
        3. otherwise if they are not equal then if start < mid then we should see on right side or if start and middle are equal  along with case that middle is greater than end then we can again check right side.
        4. Otherwise simply check left side
    - Complete Code
        
        ```java
        static int findPivotWithDuplicates(int[] arr){
            int start = 0;
            int end = arr.length - 1;
            while(start <= end){
                int mid = start + (end-start)/2;
                // 4 cases over here
                if(mid < end && arr[mid] > arr[mid+1]){
                    return mid;
                }
                if (mid > start && arr[mid] < arr[mid-1]){
                    return mid-1;
                }
        
                // if elements at middle, start and end are equal then just skip the duplicates
                if (arr[mid] == arr[start] && arr[mid] == arr[end]){
                    // skip the duplicates
        
                    // NOTE: what these elements at start and end are the pivots
                    // check if start is pivot
                    if(arr[start] > arr[start + 1]){
                        return start;
                    }
                    start++;
        
                    // end is pivot or not
                    if(arr[end] < arr[end-1]){
                        return end - 1;
                    }
                    end--;
                }
                // left side is sorted, so pivot should be in right
                else if(arr[start] < arr[mid] || (arr[start] == arr[mid] && arr[mid] > arr[end]) ){
                    start = mid + 1;
                }else{
                    end = mid - 1;
                }
            }
            return -1;
        }
        ```

    6. We get two subarrays. If subarray we are getting are lesser than equal to ones allowed to us ( m )
    7. If we are dividing into less than m pieces/subarrays then it means that individual sum array will be very large and more subarrays mean smaller sum ( overall ).
    8. But we need to reduce the sum we got (21) to something lower.
    
    NOTE : **This is where we get an idea of why we should use binary search because now we have a range between 10 and 32 which is sorted.**
    
    1. Thus we will move end = mid and again do the problem so that m = 3 this time and then since its greater than m we have (2) then we need lesser subarrays so we need to take sum a little greater than 15 thus start = mid + 1 and so on until start == end and mid = 18 ( the minimum we can get for two subarrays ).

- Code
    
    ```java
    public class splitArray {
        public static void main(String[] args){
    
        }
    
        static int splitArray(int[] nums, int m){
            int start = 0;
            int end = 0;
    
            for (int i = 0; i < nums.length ; i++){
                // search linearly for the largest term
                start = Math.max(start,nums[i]);
                end += nums[i];
            }
    
            // Binary search
            while(start < end ){
                // try for middle as potential answer
                int mid = start + (end - start)/2;
                // calculate how many pieces you can divide this
                int sum = 0;
                int pieces = 1; // least pieces we can have
                for(int num:nums){
                    if(sum+num > mid){
                        // you cannot add this element in this subarray, form a new one
                        // if we add this num in new subarray , then sum = num
                        sum = num;
                        pieces++;
                    }else{
                        sum += num;
                    }
                }
    
                if (pieces > m){
                    start = mid + 1;
                }else{
                    end = mid;
                }
            }
            return end; // start == end
        }
    
    }
    ```

    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int mySqrt(int x) {
            if (x == 0) return 0;
            int s = 1;
            int e = x;
            int ans = 0;
            while(s <= e){
                int mid = s + (e-s)/2;
                if(x/mid == mid) return mid;
                if(x/mid < mid){
                    e = mid - 1;
                }else{
                    s = mid + 1;
                    ans = mid;
                }
            }
            return ans;
        }
    }
    ```

    ```java
            while(s <= n){
                int mid = s + (n-s)/2;
                if(isBadVersion(mid)){
                    ans = mid;
                    n = mid - 1;
                }else{
                    s = mid + 1;
    ```

    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int[] twoSum(int[] numbers, int target) {
            int i = 0;
            int j = numbers.length -1;
            while(i <= j){
                if(numbers[i]+numbers[j] == target){
                    return new int[]{i+1,j+1};
                }else if(numbers[i]+numbers[j] < target){
                    i++;
                }else{
                    j--;
                }
            }
            return new int[]{-1,-1};
        }
    }
    ```

    Using Binary Search
    
    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int[] twoSum(int[] numbers, int target) {
            int start=0;
            int end=numbers.length-1;
            while(start<=end){
                int sum=numbers[start]+numbers[end];
                if(sum==target){
                    return new int[]{start+1,end+1};
                }
                else if(sum>target){
                    end=binarySearch(numbers,start+1,end-1,target-numbers[start]);
                }
                else{
                    start=binarySearch(numbers,start+1,end-1,target-numbers[end]);
                }
            }
            return new int[] {0,0};
        }
        public int binarySearch(int[] nums,int start,int end,int target){
            int mid=0;
            while(start<=end){
                mid=start+(end-start)/2;
                if(nums[mid]==target){
                    return mid;
                }
                else if(nums[mid]<target){
                    start=mid+1;
                }
                else{
                    end=mid-1;
                }
            }
            return mid;
        }
    }
    ```

    ```java
    class Solution {
        public boolean isPerfectSquare(int num) {
            long s = 1;
            long e = num;
            while(s<=e){
                long mid = s+(e-s)/2;
                if(mid*mid == num) return true;
                if(mid*mid > num){
                    e = mid -1;
                }else{
                    s = mid + 1;
                }
            }
            return false;
        }
    }
    ```

    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int arrangeCoins(int n) {
             int s = 0;
            int e = n;
            while(s <= e){
                int mid = s + (e-s)/2;
                long coins = (long) mid * (mid + 1 )/2;
                if(coins == n){
                    return mid;
                }
                if(coins < n){
                    s = mid + 1;
                }else{
                    e = mid - 1;
                }
            }
            return e;
        }
    ```

    ```java
    class Solution {
        public char nextGreatestLetter(char[] letters, char target) {
            int start = 0;
            int end = letters.length - 1;
    
            while(start <= end){
                // find the middle element
                int mid = start+(end-start)/2;
                if(target < letters[mid]){
                    end = mid - 1;
                }else {
                    start = mid + 1;
                }
            }
            return letters[start % letters.length];
        }
    }
    ```

- [Kth Missing Positive Number](https://leetcode.com/problems/kth-missing-positive-number/)
    
    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int findKthPositive(int[] arr, int k) {
            int n = arr.length;
            int start = 0, end = n-1;
            while (start <= end) {
                int mid = start + (end - start) / 2;
                if (arr[mid] - (mid + 1) < k)
                    start = mid + 1;
                else
                    end = mid - 1;
            }
            return start + k;
        }
    }
    ```
    
    - Explanation of how we reached this code
        
        # **Intuition of this Problem:**
        
        1. First thing is **how we can find number of mission element ?**, so below is the magic statement :**arr[i] - (i + 1)** : this statement will give us number of missing element before each **arr[i]** element, here **i** is nothing but **mid** used in the code.**For example, for the array [2,3,4,7,11], the number of missing positive integers before each element is [1,1,1,3,6] using above statement.**
        2. Second thing is after finding number of missing element before each element, **how we can find that element which is missing ?** :
        
        We then use binary search to find the first index **start** such that the number of missing positive integers before **arr[start]** is greater than or equal to k. Once we have found this index **start**, we know that the kth smallest missing positive integer is between **arr[start - 1]** and **arr[start]**. Therefore, we can compute the kth smallest missing positive integer as **arr[start - 1] + (k - (arr[start - 1] - (start - 1) - 1)) = start + k**.
        
        Let's break down this expression:
        
        1. **arr[start - 1]** is the last element before the kth missing positive integer, so we start with this value.
        2. **(k - (arr[start - 1] - (start - 1) - 1))** is the number of missing positive integers between **arr[start - 1]** and the kth missing positive integer. We subtract **arr[start - 1] - (start - 1) - 1** from k to account for the missing positive integers before **arr[start - 1]**. We then add this value to **arr[start - 1]** to get the kth missing positive integer.
        
        I know its bit confusing but if you will read two or three times or dry run this code to above statement then you will understand better.
        
        # **Approach for this Problem:**
        
        1. Initialize start to 0 and end to n-1, where n is the size of the input array arr.
        2. Use binary search to find the index i of the kth missing positive integer.
        3. While start is less than or equal to end, calculate the midpoint mid as start + (end - start) / 2.
        4. If the number of missing positive integers before arr[mid] is less than k, set start to mid + 1.
        5. Otherwise, set end to mid - 1.
        6. After the binary search is complete, calculate the kth missing positive integer as **start + k**, where start is the index found by binary search.
        
        For those of you who are having trouble with arr[start−1]+(k−(arr[start−1]−(start−1)−1))arr[start - 1] + (k - (arr[start - 1] - (start - 1) - 1))*arr*[*start*−1]+(*k*−(*arr*[*start*−1]−(*start*−1)−1)), take these things into consideration:
        
        - for the array `[2, 3, 4, 7, 11]`, the number of missing integers before each element is `[1, 1, 1, 3, 6]`
        - arr[i]−(i+1)arr[i] - (i + 1)*arr*[*i*]−(*i*+1) gives us the number of missing integers before index ii*i*
        - arr[start−1]−((start−1)+1)arr[start - 1] - ((start - 1) + 1)*arr*[*start*−1]−((*start*−1)+1) gives us the number of missing integers before index start−1start - 1*start*−1
        - k−(arr[start−1]−((start−1)+1))k - (arr[start - 1] - ((start - 1) + 1))*k*−(*arr*[*start*−1]−((*start*−1)+1)) gives the number of places after arr[start−1]arr[start - 1]*arr*[*start*−1] where the kth missing number exists.
        - arr[start−1]+(k−(arr[start−1]−((start−1)+1)))arr[start - 1] + (k - (arr[start - 1] - ((start - 1) + 1)))*arr*[*start*−1]+(*k*−(*arr*[*start*−1]−((*start*−1)+1))) (which is nothing but start+kstart + k*start*+*k*) gives the kth missing positive integer.
- [Search Insert Position](https://leetcode.com/problems/search-insert-position/)
    
    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int searchInsert(int[] nums, int target) {
            int s = 0;
            int e = nums.length -1;
            while(s <= e){
                int m = s + (e-s)/2;
                if(nums[m] == target){
                    return m;
                }
    
                if(nums[m] < target) s = m + 1;
                else e = m -1;
            }
            return s;
        }
    }
    ```
    
- [Peak Index in a Mountain Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/peak-index-in-a-mountain-array/)
    
    ```java
    class Solution {
        public int peakIndexInMountainArray(int[] arr) {
            int start = 0;
            int end = arr.length - 1;
            while(start < end){
                int mid = start + ( end - start ) / 2;
                if (arr[mid] > arr[mid+1]){
                    end = mid;
    
                }else{
                    start = mid + 1;
                }
            }
            return start;
        }
    }
    ```
    
- [Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-negative-numbers-in-a-sorted-matrix/)
    - with complexity O(nlogm)
        
        ```jsx
        public int countNegatives(int[][] grid) {
            int count = 0;
            int m = grid.length;
            int n = grid[0].length;
            for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
                int left = 0;
                int right = n - 1;
                while (left <= right) {
                    int mid = left + (right - left) / 2;
                    if (grid[i][mid] < 0) {
                        right = mid - 1;
                    } else {
                        left = mid + 1;
                    }
                }
                count += n - left;
            }
            return count;
        }
        ```
        
    - with Complexity O(n+m)
        
        ```jsx
        class Solution {
           public int countNegatives(int[][] grid) {
            int count = 0;
            int row = grid.length - 1;
            int col = 0;
            while (row >= 0 && col < grid[0].length) {
                if (grid[row][col] < 0) {
                    count += grid[0].length - col;
                    row--;
                } else {
                    col++;
                }
            }
            return count;
        }
        
        }
        ```

    ```jsx
    import java.util.*;
    
    public int[] intersection(int[] nums1, int[] nums2) {
        Arrays.sort(nums1);
        Set<Integer> set = new HashSet<>();
        for (int num : nums2) {
            if (binarySearch(nums1, num)) {
                set.add(num);
            }
        }
        int[] result = new int[set.size()];
        int i = 0;
        for (int num : set) {
            result[i++] = num;
        }
        return result;
    }
    
    public boolean binarySearch(int[] nums, int target) {
        int left = 0;
        int right = nums.length - 1;
        while (left <= right) {
            int mid = left + (right - left) / 2;
            if (nums[mid] == target) {
                return true;
            } else if (nums[mid] < target) {
                left = mid + 1;
            } else {
                right = mid - 1;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    ```
    
    first sorted the arrays using bubble sort and then looped through another array while using binary search to check if an element exists finally returning the array.

    ```java
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class Bianry2D {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
            int [][] arr = {
                    {10, 20, 30, 40},
                    {15, 25, 35, 45},
                    {28, 29, 37, 49},
                    {33, 34, 38, 50}
            };
            System.out.println(Arrays.toString(search(arr, 37)));
        }
    
        static int[] search(int[][] matrix, int target){
            int r = 0;
            int c = matrix.length - 1;
    
            while (r < matrix.length && c >= 0){
                if(matrix[r][c] == target){
                    return new int[]{r,c};
                }
    
                if(matrix[r][c] < target){
                    r++;
                }else{
                    c--;
                }
            }
            return new int[]{-1,-1};
        }
    }
    ```

        ```java
        public class StrictlySortedBS {
            public static void main(String[] args){
        
            }
        
            // search in the row provided between the column provided
            static int[] binarySearch(int[][] matrix, int row, int cStart, int cEnd, int target){
                while(cStart <= cEnd){
                    int mid = cStart + (cEnd - cStart)/2;
                    if(matrix[row][mid] == target){
                        return new int[]{row,mid};
                    }
                    if(matrix[row][mid] < target){
                        cStart = mid + 1;
                    }else{
                        cEnd = mid - 1;
                    }
                }
                return new int[]{-1,-1};
            }
        
            static int[] search(int[][]matrix , int target){
                int rows = matrix.length;
                int cols = matrix[0].length;
        
                if(rows == 1){
                    return binarySearch(matrix,0,0,cols-1,target);
                }
                int rStart = 0;
                int rEnd = rows - 1;
                int cMid = cols /2;
                // run loop till 2 rows remain
                while(rStart < (rEnd-1)){
                    // While its true there will  be more than 2 rows
                    int mid = rStart + (rEnd - rStart)/2;
                    if(matrix[mid][cMid] == target){
                        return new int[]{mid,cMid};
                    }
                    if(matrix[mid][cMid] < target){
                        rStart = mid + 1;
                    }else{
                        rEnd = mid -1;
                    }
        
                }
        
                // Now we have two rows
                // check whether target is in col 2 of rows
                if(matrix[rStart][cMid] == target){
                    return new int[]{rStart,cMid};
                }
                if(matrix[rStart+1][cMid] == target ){
                    return new int[]{rStart+1,cMid};
                }
        
                // search in 1st half
                if(target  <= matrix[rStart][cMid-1]){
                    return binarySearch(matrix, rStart, 0, cMid - 1, target);
                }
                // search in 2nd half
                if(target  >= matrix[rStart][cMid+1] && target <= matrix[rStart][cols-1] ){
                    return binarySearch(matrix, rStart, cMid + 1, cols - 1, target);
                }
                // search in 3rd half
                if(target  <= matrix[rStart + 1][cMid-1]){
                    return binarySearch(matrix, rStart + 1, 0, cMid - 1, target);
                }
                // search in 4th half
                else {
                    return binarySearch(matrix, rStart + 1, cMid + 1, cols - 1, target);
                }
        
            }
        }
        ```

- Stable and Unstable Sorting
    1. When the sorting keeps the equal values as they were after sorting it’s **Stable Sorting**. 
    2. For red 10 was after black as its after sorting as well.
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20256.png)
    
    1. Otherwise if red comes before black 10 then it does not kept the equal entity order as it was before then it’s **Unstable Sorting** .
- Code
    
    ```java
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class BubbleSort {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
            int[] arr = {1,2,3,4,5};
    bubbleSort(arr);
            System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr));
        }
        static void bubbleSort(int[] arr){
            boolean swapped;
    //        run the steps n-1 times
            for(int i = 0; i < arr.length ; i++){
                // for each step the max value comes at the last respective index
                swapped = false;
                for(int j = 1; j < arr.length - i; ++j){
                    // swap if item is smaller than the previous item
                    if(arr[j] < arr[j-1]){
                        // swap
                        int temp = arr[j];
                        arr[j] = arr[j-1];
                        arr[j-1] = temp;
                        swapped = true;
                    }
                }
    
                if(!swapped) break;
            }
        }
    }
    ```

- code
    
    ```java
    import java.lang.reflect.Array;
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class selectionSort {
         static public void main(String[] args){
             int[] arr = {5,4,3,2,1};
    selectionSort(arr);
             System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr));
         }
         static void selectionSort(int[] arr){
             for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
                 // find the max item in the remaining array and swap with correct index
                 int last = arr.length - i - 1;
                 int maxIndex =getMaxIndex(arr,0,last);
    swap(arr,maxIndex,last);
             }
         }
    
        static int getMaxIndex(int[] arr, int start, int end) {
             int max = start;
            for (int i = start; i <= end ; i++) {
                if(arr[max] < arr[i]){
                    max = i;
                }
            }
            return max;
        }
    
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
             int temp = arr[first];
             arr[first] = arr[second];
             arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    
    ```

Notes

- code
    
    ```java
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class InsertionSort {
    
        static public void main(String[] args){
            int[] arr = {2,-32,0,23,1};
    insertion(arr);
            System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr));
        }
        static void insertion(int[] arr){
            for(int i = 0; i < arr.length - 1;++i){
                for(int j = i+1; j > 0; j--){
                    if(arr[j] < arr[j-1]){
    swap(arr,j,j-1);
                    }else{
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
            int temp = arr[first];
            arr[first] = arr[second];
            arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    
    ```
    

## Cyclic Sort ( Important )

[cyclic_sort_notes.pdf](cyclic_sort_notes.pdf)

[Cyclic Sort.pdf](Cyclic_Sort.pdf)

- Concept
    1. We check the first value and swap it for its correct index.
    2. Until we get the correct element at first index or index 0.
    3. Correct index for given element is index - 1. For 3 correct index is 2 if array is from range 1 to N.

**If range from 1 to N is given only use cyclic sort**

- Time Complexity
    1. Complexity is linear O(N) as we make N-1 comparisons for swapping and then N swaps for checking if every element is at correct index.
    2. N-1 + N = 2N - 1 or O(N)
- code
    
    ```java
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class CyclicSort {
        static public void main(String[] args){
            int[] arr = {5,4,3,2,1};
    cyclicSort(arr);
            System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr));
        }
        static void cyclicSort(int[] arr){
            int i = 0;
            while(i < arr.length){
                int correct = arr[i] - 1;
                if(arr[i] != arr[correct]){
    swap(arr,i,correct);
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
            }
        }
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
            int temp = arr[first];
            arr[first] = arr[second];
            arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    
    ```

## Merge Sort

[Merge Sort.pdf](Merge_Sort.pdf)

### Steps

1. Divide array into two parts 
2. Sort the sub parts using recusrion then 
3. Merge sorted parts using 2 pointers approach.

![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20270.png)

1. Since its recursion so after first iteration we are gonna seperate the array only to sort and merge again. 
2. Base condition is when we have only on element left.
    
    ```jsx
    import java.util.Arrays;
    
    public class MergeSort {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
            int[] arr = {5,4,3,2,1};
            arr = mergeSort(arr);
            System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr));
        }
    
        static int[] mergeSort(int[] arr){
            if(arr.length == 1){
                return arr;
            }
            int mid = arr.length / 2;
            int[] left = mergeSort(Arrays.copyOfRange(arr,0,mid));
            int[] right = mergeSort(Arrays.copyOfRange(arr,mid,arr.length));
            return merge(left,right);
        }
    
        static int[] merge(int[] first, int[] second) {
            int[] mix = new int[first.length + second.length];
            int i = 0;
            int j = 0;
            int k = 0; // Pointer for mix array to contain final answers
    
            while(i < first.length && j < second.length){
                if(first[i] < second[j]){
                    mix[k] = first[i];
                    i++;
                }else{
                    mix[k] = second[j];
                    j++;
                }
                k++;
            }
    
            // it may be possible that one of the array is not complete
    
            // copy the remaining elements
            while(i < first.length){
                mix[k] = first[i];
                i++;
                k++;
            }
    
            while(j < second.length){
                mix[k] = second[j];
                j++;
                k++;
            }
            return mix;
        }
    }
    ```
    
- Time Complexity
    1. At each level total elements being merged are always N.
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20271.png)
        
    2. O(nlogn)
- In Place Sorting
    
    > means using original array and do not creating new arrays
    > 
    
    ```jsx
    static void mergeSortInPlace(int[] arr, int s, int e){
            if(e-s == 1){
                return ;
            }
            int mid = s + (e-s)/2;
            mergeSortInPlace(arr,s,mid);
            mergeSortInPlace(arr,mid,e);
            mergeInPlace(arr,s,mid,e);
        }
    
        static void mergeInPlace(int[] arr, int s, int m, int e) {
            int[] mix = new int[e-s];
            int i = s;
            int j = m;
            int k = 0; // Pointer for mix array to contain final answers
    
            while(i < m && j < e){
                if(arr[i] < arr[j]){
                    mix[k] = arr[i];
                    i++;
                }else{
                    mix[k] = arr[j];
                    j++;
                }
                k++;
            }
    
            // it may be possible that one of the array is not complete
    
            // copy the remaining elements
            while(i < m){
                mix[k] = arr[i];
                i++;
                k++;
            }
    
            while(j < e){
                mix[k] = arr[j];
                j++;
                k++;
            }
            for (int l = 0; l < mix.length; l++) {
                arr[s+l] = mix[l];
            }
        }
    ```

## Sorting Questions

### Missing Number ( Easy )

[Missing Number - LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/missing-number/)

- Problem
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20272.png)
    
- Approach
    
    ### Case 1  (When N is available in the array )
    
    1. Here index == element itself as we start from zero till N.
    2. We sort the array and ignore the element whose index does not exist like 4 index should be 3 but there is no index 3.
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20273.png)
        
    
    ### Case 2 ( When n is not there )
    
    N is included because we are asked to check numbers from 0 to N ( size = 4 ) then 4 should be there as well 
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20274.png)
    
- Code
    
    ```java
    class MissingNumber {
        public int missingNumber(int[] nums) {
            int i = 0;
            while(i < nums.length){
                int correct = nums[i];
                if(nums[i] < nums.length &&  nums[i] != nums[correct]){ // ignoring Nth element ( last )
    swap(nums,i,correct);
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
            }
    
            // Search for first missing element
            for (int index = 0; index < nums.length ; index++) {
                if(nums[index] != index){
                    return index;
                }
            }
    
    //        case 2 ( n is not available so simple return it
            return nums.length;
        }
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
            int temp = arr[first];
            arr[first] = arr[second];
            arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    ```
    

### **Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array ( Google )**

[Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array - LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-all-numbers-disappeared-in-an-array/)

- Problem
    
    Given an array `nums`
     of `n`
     integers where `nums[i]`
     is in the range `[1, n]`
    , return *an array of all the integers in the range*
     `[1, n]`
     *that do not appear in*
     `nums`
    .
    
- Approach
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20275.png)
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20276.png)
    
    Now we have to find missing → Numbers which are not at correct index are the missing ones as since array is sorted so they should be at their relevant index since they are not thus they are missing ones.
    
- Code
    
    ```java
    import java.util.ArrayList;
    import java.util.List;
    
    public class AllMissingNumbers {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
    
        }
    
        static List<Integer>  findDisappearedNumbers(int[] arr){
            int i = 0;
            while(i < arr.length){
                int correct = arr[i] - 1;
                if( arr[i] != arr[correct]){
    swap(arr,i,correct);
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
            }
    
            //just find missing elements
            List<Integer> ans = new ArrayList<>();
            for(int index = 0; index < arr.length ; index++){
                if(arr[index] != index+1){
                    ans.add(index+1);
                }
            }
            return ans;
    
        }
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
            int temp = arr[first];
            arr[first] = arr[second];
            arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    
    ```
    

### Find the duplicate Number ( Amazon )

[Find the Duplicate Number - LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-the-duplicate-number/)

- Problem
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20277.png)
    
    1.Find the duplicate one here 
    
- Approach
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20278.png)
    
    1. In this case when we do as done previously compare elements with correct index if not swap.
    2. But here one more condition is added i.e check if element at current index ≠ element at correct index then we swap and if its not true then else is we found our answer.
- Code
    
    ```java
    public class FindDuplicate{
        public static void main(String[] args){
            int[] arr = {3,2,5,1,4,3};
            System.out.println(findDuplicate(arr));
        }
    
        static int findDuplicate(int[] nums){
            int i = 0;
            while(i < nums.length){
                if(nums[i] != i + 1){
                    int correct = nums[i] - 1;
                    if(nums[i] != nums[correct]){
    swap(nums,i,correct);
                    }else{
                        return nums[i];
                    }
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
    
            }
            return -1;
    
        }
    
            private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
                int temp = arr[first];
                arr[first] = arr[second];
                arr[second] = temp;
            }
    }
    
    ```

- Code

    ```java
    static int[] findErrorNums(int[] nums) {
        int i = 0;
        while(i < nums.length){
                int correct = nums[i] - 1;
                if(nums[i] != nums[correct]){
    swap(nums,i,correct);
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
    
        }
    
        for (int j = 0; j < nums.length; j++) {
            if(nums[j] != j + 1 ){
                return new int[] {nums[j],j+1};
            }
        }
        return new int[] {-1,-1};
    }
    private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
        int temp = arr[first];
        arr[first] = arr[second];
        arr[second] = temp;
    }
    ```

- Code
    
    ```java
    public class SmallestMissingPositive {
        public static void main (String[] args){
    
        }
        static int firstMissingPositive(int[] nums) {
            int i = 0;
            while(i < nums.length){
                int correct = nums[i] - 1;
                if(nums[i] > 0 && nums[i] <= nums.length && nums[i] != nums[correct]){
    swap(nums,i,correct);
                }else{
                    i++;
                }
            }
    
            for(int index = 0; index < nums.length; index++){
                if(nums[index] != index + 1){
                    return index + 1;
                }
            }
    
    //        case 2
            return nums.length + 1;
    
        }
    
        private static void swap(int[] arr,int first, int second ){
            int temp = arr[first];
            arr[first] = arr[second];
            arr[second] = temp;
        }
    }
    
    ```

[Patterns.pdf](Patterns.pdf)

- Pattern 28
    
    1.Contains printing of spaces as well.
    
    ```java
    static void pattern28(int n){
        for (int row = 0; row < 2*n; row++) {
            int totalColsInRow = row > n ? 2 * n - row  : row;
            int noOfSpaces = n - totalColsInRow;
            for (int s = 0; s < noOfSpaces; s++) {
                System.out.print(" ");
            }
            for (int col = 0; col < totalColsInRow ; col++) {
                System.out.print("* ");
            }
            System.out.println();
        }
    }
    ```
    
     
    
- Pattern 30
    
    ```java
    static void pattern30(int n){
        for(int row = 1; row <= n; row++ ){
    
            for (int s = 0; s < n - row ; s++) {
                System.out.print("  ");
            }
            for (int col = row; col >= 1 ; col--) {
                System.out.print(col + " ");
            }
    
            for (int col = 2; col <= row ; col++) {
                System.out.print(col + " ");
            }
            System.out.println();
        }
    }
    ```
    
- Pattern 17
    
    ```java
    static void pattern17(int n){
        for(int row = 1; row <= 2 * n; row++ ){
            int totalColsInRow = row > n ? 2 * n - row  : row;
            int noOfSpaces = n - totalColsInRow;
            for (int s = 0; s < noOfSpaces ; s++) {
                System.out.print("  ");
            }
            for (int col = totalColsInRow; col >= 1 ; col--) {
                System.out.print(col + " ");
            }
    
            for (int col = 2; col <= totalColsInRow ; col++) {
                System.out.print(col + " ");
            }
            System.out.println();
        }
    }
    ```
    
- Pattern 31
    
    ```java
    static void pattern31(int n){
        int originalN = n;
        n = 2*n;
        for (int row = 0; row <= n; row++) {
            for (int col = 0; col <= n ; col++) {
                int atEveryIndex = originalN - Math.min(Math.min(row,col),Math.min(n-row,n - col));
                System.out.print(atEveryIndex + " ");
            }
            System.out.println();
        }
    }
    ```

    ```jsx
    public class NumbersExampleRecursion {
        public static void main(String[] args) {
            // write a function that takes in a number and prints it
            // print first 5 numbers: 1 2 3 4 5
    
            print(1);
        }
    
        static void print(int n) {
            // base condition
            if (n == 5) {
                System.out.println(5);
                return;
            }
            System.out.println(n);
    
            // recursive call
            // if you are calling a function again and again, you can treat it as a separate call in the stack
    
            // this is called tail recursion
            // this is the last function call
            print(n + 1);
        }
    }
    ```

- Examples
    - Fibonacci Numbers
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20293.png)
        
        Problem can be broken into two small parts as shown.
        
        ```jsx
        public class Fibo {
            public static void main(String[] args){
                System.out.println(fibo(6));
            }
            static int fibo (int n){
                if(n < 2){
                    return n;
                }
        
                return fibo(n-1) + fibo(n-2);
            }
        }
        ```
        
    - Binary Search ( Recursive )
        1. Since binary search can be divided into smaller problems, like dividing from mid and checking if start > mid or less and vise versa for end.
        2. That is why we can use recursion here.
        3. We are passing start and end as arguments because they are needed in future computation while mid since is not needed, so not needed to be used in arguments. Its only in function body.
        
        ```jsx
        public class recursiveBinary {
            public static void main(String[] args){
                int[] arr = {2,3,5,6,12,14,21,22};
                System.out.println(binarySearch(arr,6,0,arr.length));
            }
        
            static int binarySearch(int[] arr, int target, int s, int e){
                if(s > e){
                    return -1;
                }
                int m = s + (e - s)/2;
                if(arr[m] == target){
                    return m;
                }
                if(target < arr[m]){
                    return binarySearch(arr,target,s,m-1);
                }
                return binarySearch(arr,target,m + 1,e);
            }
        }
        ```

        $$

### Maximum Sum Subarray ( Leetcode → Medium )

1. First we can try Brute Force solution i.e to check all possible sum of elements in the array
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20296.png)
    
2. But it takes O(n2) time complexity 
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20297.png)
    
3. In this algorithm we take into account the max sum of subarray until current index.
4. Like in case of index 0 its 1 only, then for index 2 max sum can be 2 out of three subarrays [1,-3,2], [-3,2],[2].
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20298.png)
    
5. At last we compare all the subarrays we obtained from above and compare them to get max subarray i.e. [2,1]
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20299.png)
    
    It takes O(N^2) but can be converted to linear O(N).
    
6. From this algorithm we derive a rule that until current index the max subarray is either the element itself or current and previous ( Index ) max subarray. 
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20300.png)
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20301.png)
    

### Algorithm Implementation

### Two Pointer ( O(N) solution )

It has two variations 

- Slow and Fast Pointer → normally use for finding middle values like linked list mid point.
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20304.png)
    
    1. Here slow pointer takes only one step and while takes two step.
    2. The condition of checking both next and next of next is to make sure when we are at end we do not try to access an element which does not even exists.
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20305.png)
    
    - Example
        
        [Middle of a Linked List ( Slow and Fast Pointer )](https://www.notion.so/Middle-of-a-Linked-List-Slow-and-Fast-Pointer-9f6c9684afe74461b4c9ab8e34495689?pvs=21)  
        
- Front and Back pointer → Front points to Start of the array and Back points to end of the array.
    1. Let us explore an example for it.
    - Example
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20306.png)
        
        - Brute Force
            
            Plainly compare all elements with all other elements. it has time complexity of O(N^2) 
            
            We can look for an algorithm having complexity greater than NlogN as its smaller in terms time and size relations growth over time ( Time Complexity ).
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20307.png)
            
        - Binary Search
            
            > Since array is sorted so we can use Binary Search.
            > 
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20308.png)
            
            1. Start with first index , now if start + mid > target then start should be moved to right side of the array.
            2. Then we check if start + mid > target else we move mid to left so that both start and end point to same element
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20309.png)
            
            Further faster can be O(N) then nlogn 
            
        - Two Pointer
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20310.png)
            
            1. Front at start and back at end. 
            2. Were if we move front ahead we have larger sum and back behind means smaller sum.
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20311.png)
            
            ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20312.png)
            
        - Two Pointer Code
            
            ```java
            class Solution{
            	public int[] twoSum(int[] nums,int target){
            		int l = 0;
            		int r = nums.length-1;
            		while(l<r){
            				int sum = nums[l] + nums[r];
            				if(sum == target ){
            					return new int[] {l+1,r+1};
            				}else if(sum <= target){
            					l++;
            				}else{
            					r++;
            				}
            		}
            		return new int[2];
            	}
            }
            ```
            

### Floyd’s Cycle Detection ( Tortoise and Hare )

- Scenario
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20313.png)
    
    1. Normally Linked list is traversed until next null 
    2. But this fails when pointer is never null, when there is a cycle existing within there.
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20314.png)
    
- Possible Solution (linear time and space Complexity )
    1. Store nodes visited in some place and every time you move to a new node check if it is in there in visitedNodes.
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20315.png)
    
    It as linear time complexity as well as linear space complexity 
    
    ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20316.png)
    
- Floyd’s Cycle Detection
    - How it works
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20317.png)
        
        1. Has two pointer slow and fast 
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20318.png)
        
        1. Where slow one moves one node at a time and fast one with two nodes at a time.
        2. First step is to check if to loop until fast pointer is null.
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20319.png)
        
        then it means that there is no cycle.
        
        1. Otherwise if there is a cycle then slow and fast will meet each other after some time as fast takes two nodes at a time.
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20320.png)
        
        > If slow meets fast or vise versa then there exists a cycle.
        > 
        1. To find head of circle, we put slow at start of linked list and move until they both meet again and i.e Entry point of circle.
        
        ![Untitled](Learning/DSA/Java/attachments/Untitled%20321.png)
